blocks.text: Reducing hallucinations is one of the most frequently asked practical questions about fine-tuned models, and the honest answer spans several distinct levers, covered separately across earlier modules of this course, this topic pulls them together into a single practical reference for approaching the problem systematically.
No single technique eliminates hallucination entirely, the strongest results usually come from combining several of the approaches covered below rather than relying on just one.
1. The Four Main Levers
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472914646-530809504.png

Reducing hallucination generally comes down to four connected levers, the quality of training data itself, how well the model is grounded in verifiable source material, whether the training objective actively discourages unsupported claims, and whether hallucination is actually measured so progress can be tracked.
2. Cleaning Up Training Data First
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472914646-718657063.png

A model trained on examples containing unverified or incorrect claims, connecting to the dataset cleaning practices covered in an earlier module, directly learns to produce similar unsupported content, careful data verification during the cleaning stage is one of the highest-leverage, lowest-complexity ways to reduce downstream hallucination.
3. Grounding Responses in Retrieved Context
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472914646-314103171.png

Retrieval augmented fine-tuning, RAFT, covered in an earlier topic, specifically trains a model to ground its answers in provided source material and correctly ignore irrelevant distractor context, this directly reduces the kind of hallucination that comes from a model blending or fabricating information rather than citing what it was actually given.
4. Penalizing Unsupported Claims During Alignment
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472914647-276014641.png

The preference optimization methods covered in the Alignment Training module, RLHF, DPO, and related techniques, can specifically incorporate a preference signal that penalizes confidently stated but unsupported claims, directly training the model reward function to disfavor hallucinated content rather than only optimizing for general response quality.

blocks.text: 5. Teaching a Model to Say It Does Not Know

blocks.alt: Teaching a Model to Say It Does Not Know
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472914647-772711852.png

Training data that always includes a confident answer, even for genuinely ambiguous or unanswerable questions, teaches a model that confident answering is always the expected behavior, deliberately including examples where the correct response is expressing uncertainty or declining to answer teaches the model this is also a valid, sometimes preferred, response.

blocks.title: This is a genuinely underused technique in practice
blocks.content: Many training datasets are curated to only include confidently correct examples, inadvertently teaching a model that uncertainty is never an acceptable response, explicitly including well-labeled uncertain or unanswerable examples directly counters this.

blocks.text: 6. Measuring Hallucination to Track Progress
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472914647-885545776.png

The hallucination evaluation approach covered in an earlier topic, extracting and verifying individual claims against a source, should be run consistently across fine-tuning checkpoints, without measuring hallucination directly, it is easy to inadvertently make it worse while other quality metrics look fine, since general fluency and factual accuracy are genuinely independent dimensions.
7. Decoding Settings Also Matter
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785472914647-709749648.png

Beyond training-time interventions, inference-time decoding settings, covered in the earlier Text Generation topic, also affect hallucination rate, a lower sampling temperature reduces the randomness that can lead to a confidently stated but essentially random claim, though this is a smaller lever than the training-time interventions covered above.
8. There Is No Single Silver Bullet

Given hallucination has multiple distinct causes, data quality issues, weak grounding, a training objective that never penalizes overconfidence, no single technique from this topic fully solves it alone, the strongest practical results combine several levers, data cleaning, RAFT-style grounding, alignment training with a hallucination-aware preference signal, and continuous measurement.
9. Prioritizing Given Limited Time and Resources

For a team with limited time to address hallucination, data quality cleaning is usually the highest leverage first step given its relative simplicity, RAFT-style grounding is the next highest leverage step for retrieval-augmented use cases specifically, alignment training adjustments and explicit uncertainty training are valuable additional refinements once the foundational data and grounding work is in place.
Worked Example

A team notices their fine-tuned customer support model occasionally states incorrect policy details confidently. They first audit and clean their training data, finding and removing several examples with subtly incorrect information, then add RAFT-style training examples with distractor documents to strengthen grounding.

They also add training examples where the correct response is acknowledging uncertainty for genuinely ambiguous policy questions, and set up a hallucination evaluation pipeline to track claim verification rate across each subsequent training checkpoint, confirming measurable improvement rather than assuming these interventions worked.
Common Mistakes

items: Expecting a single technique, like just adding retrieval, to fully solve hallucination without addressing data quality
Never explicitly training examples where uncertainty or declining to answer is the correct response
Not measuring hallucination rate directly, missing a regression that other quality metrics would not reveal
Skipping training data verification and cleaning, the highest leverage and often cheapest intervention available

blocks.text: Practice

For a fine-tuned model use case you are familiar with, rank the four levers covered in this topic, data quality, grounding, training objective, and measurement, by which would likely provide the biggest hallucination reduction for that specific use case, and explain your reasoning.
Key Takeaway

Reducing hallucination requires combining several distinct levers rather than relying on one, cleaning training data to remove unverified claims, grounding responses through RAFT-style training, penalizing unsupported claims during alignment training, explicitly teaching a model to express uncertainty when appropriate, and continuously measuring hallucination rate to confirm these interventions are actually working rather than assuming they are.
